play.name: Will you ever play it?
play.hint: Backlog with no score or 0 h
play.explanation: You own them in some store, but they have no score or you never opened them. “No” adds them to your library as “Not interested”: you don’t see them in the list, but “Do I own it?” knows they’re yours. “Don’t import” leaves them out.

playnite.title: How do I get my Playnite library?
playnite.lead: Playnite is a free Windows program that gathers your games from Epic, GOG, Steam and other stores. Leave Steam signed out: that way it lists what you have installed.

steps.download: Download the PlayniteLibraryExport exporter from its author’s page and open the .pext file with Playnite closed.
steps.export: In Playnite: Extensions › Playnite Library Exporter › Export library now, as JSON.
steps.upload: Go back to Import and upload the file in Playnite.

ign.title: How do I get my IGN list?
ign.lead: IGN has no export button. This bookmarklet does it for you: it reads your list on IGN’s page and downloads the file, without sending anything anywhere else.
ign.dragHint: This button is used from IGN: drag it to your bookmarks bar and tap it with your IGN list open.
ign.barHint: If you don’t see the bookmarks bar: Ctrl + Shift + B in Chrome and Edge.

steps.drag: Drag this button to your browser’s bookmarks bar.
steps.open: Go to your games list on IGN, signed in.
steps.run: Tap the “Export from IGN” bookmark. Your browser downloads <mono>ign-export.json</mono>.
steps.upload: Go back to Import and upload the file in IGN.

ign.warning: The bookmarklet depends on how IGN builds its page. If IGN changes it, it may stop working: let us know and we’ll fix it.

alerts.wrongSite: This bookmarklet is used on www.ign.com: go to your IGN games list and tap it there.
alerts.signedOut: IGN didn’t give us your list. Sign in to IGN and tap the bookmarklet again.
alerts.failed: We couldn’t read your IGN list. Try again in a while.
alerts.empty: Your IGN list is empty: there’s nothing to export.
